skills.goal: Turn a list of commits (git log output) into a release section in Keep a Changelog format, written for users of the project rather than its developers.
triggers: write the changelog for these commits
draft release notes from this git log
skills.description: Turns git log output into a user-facing Keep a Changelog release section (Added/Changed/Fixed…, breaking changes first). Use when the user says "write the changelog for these commits", "draft release notes from this git log", or "update CHANGELOG.md for version X".

skills.goal: Write a git commit message for a diff, following Conventional Commits and the house rules, so history is greppable and changelogs can be generated from it.
triggers: write a commit message for this diff
what should the commit message be?
commit this change with a good message
skills.description: Writes a Conventional Commits message for a diff: type(scope): subject header, a body that explains why, and a BREAKING CHANGE footer when needed. Use when the user asks "write a commit message for this diff", "what should the commit message be?" or "commit this change with a good message".

skills.goal: Explain a standard 5-field cron expression field by field and list its next run times from a given starting time, computed carefully rather than guessed.
triggers: what does this cron expression mean?
skills.description: Explains a standard 5-field cron expression field by field, summarises it in plain English, and works out its next 3 run times from a given "now". Use when asked "what does this cron expression mean?", "when will '<cron>' run next?", or "explain this crontab line".

skills.goal: Guide building FastAPI applications: project layout, settings, schemas, dependency injection, auth, database integration, testing and production practices.
triggers: add auth to my FastAPI project
how should I structure this FastAPI service?
skills.description: Expert guidance for building FastAPI applications including API design, authentication, database integration, dependency injection, testing, and production best practices. Use when building or working with FastAPI projects.

skills.goal: Before writing a new skill or starting a repetitive workflow from scratch, check whether a skill for the task already exists in the skill-factory marketplace, and tell the user how to install the best match.
triggers: what skills do we have for <topic>?
the user asks you to write a new skill (check for an existing one first)
skills.description: Searches the skill-factory marketplace catalog for an existing skill that fits a task and gives the exact /plugin install command for the best match. Use when the user asks "is there a skill for <task>?", "find a skill that can <task>", "what skills do we have for <topic>?", or asks you to write a new skill (check first).

skills.goal: File a LeetCode solution into the CS_basics repo the way existing ones are filed.
triggers: add this solution and update the README
skills.description: File a LeetCode solution into this repo the way the existing ones are filed — find the problem's real slug, write the Python file in the house layout (problem docstring, V0 with an IDEA block and a time/space line), smoke-test it against the examples, and insert the README row. Use when asked to "add LC <number>", to file a problem just solved in a weekly contest, to turn a pasted draft into a committed solution, or to wire an existing solution file into README. Triggers - "add LC 4038 to Hash_table", "/lc-add 239 Sliding_Window", "add this solution and update the README", "file yesterday's contest Q1".

skills.goal: Coach a FAANG-style coding interview: score a solution on the six-point scale, write the interviewer's debrief, teach the fundamentals, dry-run code and recommend sibling problems.
triggers: what should I do after LC 239?
skills.description: FAANG coding-interview coach. Scores a solution the way an interviewer does on the six-point scale (SH/H/LH/LNH/NH/SNH), writes the debrief packet from the interviewer's side of the table, teaches the DSA fundamentals underneath, dry-runs code out loud, names the one line that blocks the optimal complexity, and recommends the sibling problems to drill next. Use when preparing for or debriefing a LeetCode-style SWE interview — "review my solution", "would this pass?", "what's my verdict?", "how would an interviewer see this?", "why is this O(n^2)?", "mock interview me", "what should I do after LC 239?".

skills.goal: Let the agent file a short structured report ("papercut") whenever a skill, script or tool misbehaves, is confusing, or needs a workaround, so the owner can fix it. Use it even when the agent recovered on its own.
triggers: a skill's instructions were wrong, stale or ambiguous
a script or command a skill told you to run failed or returned something unexpected
you needed a workaround to finish the user's task
skills.description: Files a short structured papercut report when a skill, script or tool misbehaves, is confusing, or needs a workaround, even if you recovered. Use when skill instructions were wrong, stale or ambiguous, a command it told you to run failed or surprised you, you needed a workaround, or the user says "log a papercut for <skill>".

skills.goal: Review Python code for quality, bugs, security and best practices, in a fixed report format.
triggers: what's wrong with this Python file?
skills.description: Provides comprehensive Python code review with focus on quality, bugs, security, and best practices. Use when reviewing Python code, functions, or modules for quality assessment.
